subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-auth embedded dispatch ship as the PR's core claude-cli policy plus public PluginRuntime eligibility method, or should the eligibility capability move behind the provider-owned CLI backend contract first?
rationale: Both implementations can fix the observed bug, but the choice determines a shipped plugin API, provider ownership, future CLI-provider extensibility, and the compatibility contract for routing and timeout defaults.

options.title: Move to provider capability
options.body: Put subscription-dispatch eligibility on the Claude CLI backend/provider contract while retaining one generic shared resolver for dispatch and timeout budgeting.

options.title: Approve the current core seam
options.body: Accept the hard-coded core provider set and public runtime helper as intentional supported contracts, with explicit compatibility ownership and upgrade coverage.

options.title: Pause the broad runtime API
options.body: Narrow the change until maintainers agree on a reusable embedded-helper dispatch contract rather than shipping a provisional public seam.

recommendation.title: Move to provider capability
recommendation.body: Put subscription-dispatch eligibility on the Claude CLI backend/provider contract while retaining one generic shared resolver for dispatch and timeout budgeting.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is repository-wide provider/runtime API direction rather than an active-memory implementation detail, and the existing same-head review routed that decision here.
